sentences.text: We have heard the counsel for the parties and gone through the evidence.
12. As per evidence the applicant has not proved on file that there was total loss of the vehicle

The applicant has submitted on record estimate in the sum of Rs.24 Rs.24,14,245/- on account of repair of the vehicle, Rs.3,10,000/ Rs.3,10,000/- repair body + labour, the estimate cost of repairs in the sum of Rs.24,14,245/

On the other hand the responden respondent in the policy has assessed the ID IDV of the vehicle to the tune of Rs. 17,00,000/-
17,00,000/ and the surveyor appointed after getting information of the accident assessed the value of loss of the vehicle to the tune of Rs.9,93,000/ Rs.9,93,000/-.

Thus there is a difference of Rs.
Rs 15,00,000/-..

The applicant has not produced the sale letter of the vehicle so as to compare the amount assessed by the authorized workshop with the total value of the vehicle, besides it is an established fact that it is the prerogative of the insurance company to assess IDV of the vehicle, no doubt the policy has to be signed by the owner of the vehicle too but it does not mean that in fact the IDV assessed by the insurance company is always correct.

In these circumstances we are of the considered opinion opinion that the amount of loss to the applicant due to accident of the vehicle has assessed by the authorized workshop needs to be kept in view to quantify the compensation in the interest of justice.
Besides admittedly the applicant had given information of the the accident after 15 days thus it becomes clear that he has violated terms and conditions of the policy.

13. In Amalendu Sahoo Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. II (2010) CPJ (9) (SC) the vehicle was not used for personal cause but was used for transportatio transportation of passengers by way of being hired.
